title: Home & Garden Ecommerce Benchmarks for 2026
summary: Conversion rate, AOV and bounce rate benchmarks for the Home and Garden ecommerce category for 2026.
body_markdown:
## **CVR Falls in Q3 and Trails 2025; AOV Now Down 3.3% Year-Over-Year**


The benchmarks:[1.65% median CVR](https://getshogun.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-conversion-rate) ,[$379 median AOV](https://getshogun.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-average-order-value) . The 25th–75th percentile AOV range is $196–$831. Q3 was a difficult quarter for Home & Garden: CVR fell 14.7% from Q2 among stores active in both quarters, against a flat seasonal baseline (+0.2%) over the same quarters in 2025. Order value no longer provides an offset — same-store matched AOV is down 3.3% year over year.


Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date Ecommerce Benchmark Reports (January–September 2026), Home & Garden.


2026 has been softer than 2025 for Home & Garden on conversion. Every month from January through September came in below its 2025 equivalent, and the gap held through Q3: July (1.48%), August (1.37%) and September (1.54%) all trailed the same months of 2025 (1.61%, 1.99% and 1.62%). Bounce rate has moved the other way, from 42–46% across January–September 2025 to 46–53% over the same months of 2026. More visitors are arriving and leaving without engaging.


As more of 2026 has come in, the order-value picture has changed. On a same-store matched basis, Home & Garden AOV is now 3.3% below the prior year ($413 to $400), and it slipped 3.4% from Q2 to Q3 ($393 to $380 across 316 stores). Every month from June through September 2026 came in below the same month of 2025.


There is one notable exception within the period: November and December 2025 posted CVR of 2.43% and 2.46% — the two highest months in the 21-month window. But that spike came with a corresponding AOV dip, suggesting gift-oriented purchasing at lower price points rather than a broad-based strengthening.


> CVR is running below 2025 levels for Home & Garden in every month of 2026 — and on a matched-store basis, AOV now trails the prior year too. Both metrics are pointing the same way.


## Conversion Rate Benchmark — 2026 Year to Date


The median Home & Garden conversion rate from January through September 2026 was 1.65%, placing it in the lower-middle tier of the 10 published industries — just below Apparel & Accessories (1.76%).


n=803 active Shopify stores, January–September 2026. Stores with CVR below 0.1% or above 25% excluded. Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date CVR Benchmark Report.


Home & Garden sits alongside Apparel as a category where shoppers browse extensively before committing. The purchase decision for outdoor furniture, kitchen appliances, or renovation materials involves more research and deliberation than a repeat-purchase category like health products or food.


> Home & Garden’s median bounce rate of 50.1% from January through September 2026 sits right at the dataset-wide median — but it has been climbing, reaching 53.4% in August. Visitors who stay are engaged, but a growing share are leaving at the first page.


## **CVR & Bounce Rate Trend — January 2025 through September 2026**


The chart below shows monthly median CVR and bounce rate for active Home & Garden stores. Twenty-one months of data makes the 2026 shift visible against a full year of 2025 baseline.


n=56–82 active stores per month. Each month measured on its own; CVR filter 0.1%–25% per site per month. Source: Shogun session and conversion tracking, Home & Garden.


CVR ran between 1.79% and 2.13% across H1 2025. Through 2026 it has held in a lower 1.37%–1.73% band, and no month has come in above its 2025 equivalent. The November–December 2025 spike (2.43% and 2.46%) stands out as the strongest CVR stretch in the entire 21-month window — but it didn’t carry forward into 2026.


Bounce rate has been climbing steadily throughout the period, rising from ~42–44% in early 2025 to ~49–53% in Q3 2026. The direction is consistent and the magnitude is significant — Q3 2026 ran roughly 5–7 percentage points above Q3 2025.


## **Average Order Value Benchmark — 2026 Year to Date**


The 2026 year-to-date median AOV for Home & Garden was $379, based on period order totals across 339 qualifying stores.


This data set is separate from the CVR cohort above — it covers anonymized full-store order data rather than Shogun page sessions, and uses different qualifying criteria.


January–September 2026, n=339 stores with at least 375 orders; AOV above $5,000 excluded. Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date AOV Benchmark Report, Home & Garden.


## **AOV Trend — June 2025 through September 2026**


The chart below tracks monthly median AOV for Home & Garden stores, with each month measured on its own (284–337 stores per month). The trend starts in June 2025 because store coverage in the order data was much thinner before then.


n=284–337 stores per month; each month measured on its own (stores with at least 50 orders that month, AOV $1–$5,000). Source: Shogun AOV benchmark data, Home & Garden.


AOV was strongest in summer 2025 ($385–$407 from June through September), a pattern consistent with summer home improvement and outdoor purchasing. It declined through fall, dropping to $327 in December — the lowest point in the 16-month window. 2026 has run in a $347–$381 range, with July 2026 ($381) the high point of the year, but every month from June through September 2026 came in below the same month of 2025.


On a matched same-store basis (n=249 stores active in both January–September 2025 and January–September 2026), median AOV moved from $413 to $400 — a −3.3% year-over-year decline. That figure is a better measure of per-store change than the monthly trend, because it follows the same stores across both periods.


## **What CVR and AOV Are Saying Together**


Earlier in 2026, Home & Garden’s story was a two-track one: CVR softer against 2025, AOV moving the other way. With data through September, both metrics now point in the same direction.


CVR is down in every month of 2026 compared to the same month in 2025, and it fell 14.7% from Q2 to Q3 among stores active in both quarters — against a flat seasonal baseline a year earlier. Monthly bounce rate is running 5–7 percentage points higher than in 2025. Those trends point the same way: fewer visitors are engaging with the site, and more are leaving without converting.


AOV no longer provides the offset it did earlier in the year. On a same-store matched basis, median AOV is down 3.3% year over year ($413 to $400 across 249 stores) and slipped 3.4% from Q2 to Q3. The decline is modest, but it means softer conversion isn’t being made up by larger baskets.


The November–December 2025 data is worth examining as a specific pattern. Those months posted CVR of 2.43% and 2.46% — the strongest in the trend window — while AOV dropped to $356 and $327 respectively. Higher conversions at lower basket sizes is consistent with gift-oriented purchasing: shoppers converting more readily on smaller home goods and decorative items during the holiday period, rather than the larger considered purchases (furniture, appliances, renovation supplies) that drive AOV the rest of the year.


> CVR trailing 2025 levels, with AOV slightly below the prior year, is now the category pattern. If your numbers match that shape, you’re tracking with the market. If your AOV is growing while conversion softens, you’re ahead of the category on order value.


## **A Note on Sub-Markets Within Home & Garden**


The $379 median is a useful reference point — but the P25-to-P75 range tells an equally important story. The middle 50% of Home & Garden stores in this dataset have an AOV somewhere between $196 and $831. That’s a $635 spread within a single category benchmark — wider than either of the other two largest categories by sample size (Apparel & Accessories and Beauty & Personal Care).


That range reflects the breadth of what “Home & Garden” contains. A store selling garden tools and seed packets operates on very different economics than one selling high-end outdoor furniture or professional kitchen equipment. Conversion rates across these sub-markets will differ just as significantly, because the purchase decision for a $30 item and a $1,200 item are not comparable experiences.


> The $379 median is a benchmark for the category. Your relevant benchmark is the sub-market you actually compete in — which may sit well above or below the headline figure.


The trend data — CVR trailing 2025 levels, bounce rate rising, and AOV slightly below the prior year on a matched basis — is likely more actionable than where your AOV lands relative to $379. Understanding which direction each metric is moving, and how that compares to the category pattern, matters more than the benchmark number alone.
